transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, um, well, I guess I came in because... well, my eating just went completely off the rails. And you have to understand, that is incredibly out of character for me. In my job—I do project management—everything is about metrics and tracking and staying ahead of the curve, and I usually apply that exact same methodology to my diet, too. I had this whole system for tracking my macros and my meals, perfectly optimized. 

But recently, I just... I completely stopped caring about my food tracking altogether. I mean, I was skipping real meals for days at a time. Literally days. I'd just be going and going, and I was basically just living on iced coffee and these chalky protein bars, and even then, I'd only eat one if it was sitting right in front of me on my desk and I happened to glance at it. It just felt like sitting down to eat was a complete waste of time, or I just didn't have the appetite for it at all, I don't even know. 

And the crazy part is, I didn't even notice what it was doing to my body until I was getting dressed for a pitch the other morning and my clothes were just hanging loose on me. Like, really loose, bagging around the knees and the waist. I had to pull my belt two notches tighter than my usual spot just to keep my slacks up, and that was the first time I actually stopped and realized how much weight I'd dropped without even trying or noticing. So, yeah, that's... that's why I'm here. Because losing control of a baseline metric like that, letting a system fail without even realizing it, it just really threw me.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or not getting pleasure from activities that you usually enjoy?

Yeah, actually, that's... that's a huge part of it, too. It’s not just the food tracking, which, like I said, was a whole system I just abandoned. It’s everything else, too. I mean, usually, I have a very structured weekend. I like to get out, clear my head, you know? I usually go hiking every Saturday morning—there’s this trail up near the ridge that I’ve practically memorized, and I always take my camera because I do a lot of landscape photography. I’ll spend hours editing those photos on Sunday afternoons, adjusting the exposure, playing with the color balance, really getting into the weeds of it. It’s how I decompress from the week. 

But lately? I haven't even taken my boots out of the closet. The thought of packing my gear, driving to the trailhead... it just feels like climbing Mount Everest. I just look at my camera bag sitting by the door and feel absolutely nothing. No desire to touch it. And I haven't wanted to edit any of the backlog of photos I have sitting on my hard drive, either. 

And it’s not just that. I have this woodworking project out in the garage—I'm building this mid-century modern credenza, walnut veneer, really intricate joinery—and I haven't even turned on the lights out there in weeks. I used to spend hours out there, measuring twice, cutting once, getting the sanding perfectly smooth. It used to keep me so grounded, you know? Like a physical manifestation of progress that I could control. But now, the garage is just gathering dust. I haven't wanted to hike, edit photos, log my meals, or even touch that credenza. It’s just so strange because those are the things that usually keep me sane, keep me anchored, and now they just feel like... I don't know, like obligations I can't even fathom fulfilling. It's like someone just flipped a switch and drained all the color out of my hobbies.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah. Yeah, I have. It’s... it’s been really bad. And I can actually pinpoint exactly when it started, too, because, like I said, I track things. We had this huge quarterly review meeting—I was the lead on this massive infrastructure rollout, a project I had been living and breathing for six months. I had all the projections, the risk mitigation strategies, everything was color-coded and mapped out on this beautiful Gantt chart. And then the project sponsor, this VP who barely even reads the weekly briefs, just completely tore into my timeline. He questioned my judgment in front of the entire steering committee. He basically insinuated I didn't know how to allocate resources. 

And normally, I would just take that, pivot, draft a rebuttal memo with the updated metrics, and handle it. That’s what a project manager does. But this time... it was like the bottom just completely dropped out. I didn't even argue. I just packed up my laptop, went home, and I sat in my apartment. And I just felt so... hollow. And ashamed. Like this deep, heavy shame that just settled right in my chest. 

And since then, it’s just been every single day. I wake up and I just feel this crushing weight. I’ve been sitting on my couch, literally crying over routine emails. Emails! Just standard update requests that I normally would have blasted out in two minutes without even thinking about it. Now I look at my inbox and I just start sobbing because it all feels so pointless and I feel so entirely incompetent. It’s not just a bad day here or there, it’s this constant, suffocating feeling from the minute I wake up until I finally manage to pass out at night. I just feel completely and utterly hopeless about everything.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your energy levels or felt unusually fatigued, even when you haven't been doing much?

No, actually. I mean, I know that sounds weird given everything else I just told you, but no, I haven't really felt tired or fatigued at all. If anything, it's almost the opposite, or maybe just... disconnected? Like, I told you about how I haven't been doing my hobbies, the photography and the woodworking, and how I've just been sitting on the couch crying over emails, but it's not because my body feels physically exhausted. It's not like my muscles are heavy or I need to sleep for twelve hours a day. 

It's more like a mental paralysis, you know? Like the engine is still running, maybe even idling a little too high sometimes, but the transmission is completely shot so the car won't actually move forward. I'm just sitting there, vibrating with all this awful, hopeless energy, but I can't direct it toward anything productive. So, no, I wouldn't say my energy levels have decreased. I don't feel physically drained or fatigued in that classic sense where you just want to sleep all the time. I'm just completely stuck.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, my focus is... well, it's intense, if anything. Like, I was mentioning that VP who tore into my timeline at the quarterly review? I can still picture the exact slide that was on the screen when he did it—Slide 42, Resource Allocation and Critical Path Dependencies. I can remember the font, the specific shade of blue I used for the Gantt chart bars, the way the projector was humming in the background... I've been replaying that exact moment in my head over and over and over again, dissecting every single word he said, every inflection, trying to figure out where the flaw was in my logic. 

So it's not that I can't focus. I'm hyper-focused. It's just that my focus is entirely consumed by this massive, overwhelming sense of failure and dread. I can sit on the couch for hours, staring at a single email from a vendor, just completely fixated on how inadequate I am to even draft a response. It's like my brain is a laser pointer, but it's just burning a hole into the same terrible spot over and over again. As for making decisions, I mean, I'm not really making any right now because I'm not doing anything. I'm just existing in this awful space. But the cognitive ability to think? It's there. It's just... it's just hijacked by all this other stuff. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble thinking clearly or focusing, not in the way you mean. It's just that what I'm focusing on is entirely unproductive and miserable.
Have you had a depressed mood most of the time for at least the past two years, even if it wasn't as severe as what you're experiencing now?

Two years? Oh, no. No, definitely not two years. I mean, I'm a project manager, right? I live and die by timelines, so I can tell you exactly when this all started. Like I said, it was that quarterly review meeting with the VP. That was... God, what month are we in? That was exactly three months ago. 

Before that, I was—I was fine. I was more than fine, actually. I was operating at absolute peak efficiency. I was managing that infrastructure rollout, I was hitting all my milestones, I was going to the gym four days a week, I was doing my woodworking on the weekends... I wasn't depressed at all. I was actually feeling really good about where my life was heading. 

But then that meeting happened. And that VP just ripped my timeline apart in front of the steering committee, and that's when the bottom dropped out. That's when this... this heavy, hollow, ashamed feeling just settled into my chest. And it's been exactly like this, this constant, suffocating dread where I can't even look at my email without crying, for the last three months. It hasn't let up for a single day since that meeting. But before that? No. I wasn't feeling down or depressed at all. It's just been this unbroken, miserable stretch for the last three months.
